points.description: States that a data member can be accessed from any member function of the class (class-wide scope), not only from the function where it is used. Equivalent wording such as 'available throughout the class' is acceptable.
points.partial_credit: Award half marks if the answer says data members are accessible from more than one member function but does not make clear that they are accessible from any member function of the class.

levels.says: Says data members can be accessed from more than one member function, but does not clearly state that access extends to any member function of the class.

points.description: States that a local variable can only be accessed inside the member function that defines or declares it (function-only scope). Equivalent wording such as 'it exists only within that function' is acceptable.
points.partial_credit: Award half marks if the answer says local variables are limited to a function but does not make clear that it is only the member function that defines them.

levels.says: Says local variables are limited to a function, but does not clearly state that access is restricted to the member function that defines them.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both scope differences: data members are accessible from any member function of the class, while local variables are accessible only inside the member function that defines them. Award half of a point's marks when the answer gives the correct broader or narrower scope but does not make the 'any member function' or 'only the defining function' distinction clear. No marks for vague statements about variables that do not identify the access or scope difference.
